title: FieldDesigner draws a delete action on system fields and silently drops the click — handleDelete returns before the confirm dialog, with no message anywhere
body:
Surfaced while implementing objectui#8060 (dev seat, session `session_01YBWFb5YgMU5dw8p2VKj16S`). ⛔ Unassigned; grading and `domain:*` are triage's. ⛔ NOT fixed in objectui#8060's PR — out of that card's scope, which is the field-type flattening.

## Measured

`packages/plugin-designer/src/FieldDesigner.tsx`:

```ts
const handleDelete = useCallback(async (record: Record<string, unknown>) => {
  const field = fields.find((f) => f.name === record.name);
  if (!field || field.isSystem) return;      // ← silent no-op
  const confirmed = await confirmDialog.confirm(...);
  ...
}, [fields, onFieldsChange, confirmDialog, t]);
```

The delete affordance is wired at the GRID level, not per row:

```tsx
onDelete={readOnly ? undefined : handleDelete}
```

`ObjectGrid` takes a single `onDelete` for the whole grid (`packages/plugin-grid/src/ObjectGrid.tsx`, `onDelete?: (record: any) => void`) and derives `{ update: !!onEdit, delete: !!onDelete }`, so the row action is rendered for EVERY row including system fields.

⇒ **Clicking delete on a system field does nothing at all** — no confirm dialog, no banner, no toast, no console message. The author clicks a button that is drawn as available and gets no response, and nothing anywhere says why.

## Why this is worth a card rather than a shrug

It is the small end of the family this repo keeps finding: an affordance that is offered and then silently declines. The `readOnly` case is handled honestly (the operations are withheld, so no button is drawn); the `isSystem` case draws the button and drops the click. The two states differ in the code and do not differ on screen.

`isSystem` is also the flag the drawer form uses to disable `name` and `type` — so the concept "this field's structure is not the designer's to change" already exists and is already rendered in one place. Delete is the one place it is enforced invisibly.

## Not asserting a direction

Three that occur to me, none ruled here and none costed:

- Withhold the row's delete action for system fields (needs per-row operation gating, which `ObjectGrid`'s grid-level `onDelete` does not offer today — that may be the real blocker and may make this a `plugin-grid` card rather than a `plugin-designer` one).
- Show the existing confirm dialog's error surface, or a toast, saying a system field cannot be deleted.
- Leave the behaviour and state it — the weakest, since the button still lies.

## Scope of the duplicate search behind this filing

Bounded, and said so rather than implied: the 500 most recent `plugin`-labelled issues in **all** states (5 pages of 100 via the REST list endpoint) were scanned by TITLE for `FieldDesigner`/`field designer` intersected with `delete`/`system`/`remove` — zero hits, with a lit control on the same command shape (`designer` matched 11 rows). Issue BODIES were not searched and the label scope was not widened, so this is a targeted read and not an exhaustive one.

## Related

objectui#8060 (surfaced it) · objectui#6044 (the card that made `isSystem` read the spec spelling `system`, i.e. why system fields are correctly identified here at all).
